chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maymūn al-Qaddāḥ, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
When death came upon one of the members of his household, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام would say to him: “Say:”

There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens, and Lord of the seven earths, and whatever is between them, and Lord of the mighty Throne; and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
Then when the sick person said it, he would say to him: “Go, and there is no harm upon you.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: When he has passed away, then his eyes should be closed, his mouth should be shut, his hands should be extended to his sides, his legs should be stretched out if they are drawn up, his jaws should be tied with a bandage to his head, and a cloth should be spread over him by which he is covered.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, referred to by his title Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.الْحَلِيمُ: the Forbearing, one of the divine attributes mentioned in the supplication
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ: the mighty Throne, expressing Allah’s supreme lordship
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ritual washing, mentioned in the chapter heading regarding the deceased
key_terms.الْمَرِيضُ: the sick person, here meaning the one nearing death
key_terms.قَضَى نَحْبَهُ: he passed away; his death occurred
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: the declaration of tawhid affirming that none is worthy of worship but Allah

ai.seo_question: What should be recited to a dying person, and what should be done immediately after death in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes what should be recited to a dying person and mentions practical acts to be done immediately after death. It combines dhikr of tawhid and divine praise with funeral etiquette and rulings concerning the handling of the deceased.
